source_text: ἡνίκα δεῖ τοῖς ἀξίοις ἐκφαίνειν. τὸν δὲ Πέτρον, ὡς προείρηται, γράψαι· ἀπεστάλη ἀπ' οὐρανοῦ τὸ πνεῦμα· νοείσθω, ᾧ τρόπῳ νοεῖται τό· ἀπεστάλη ὁ υἱός. ὡς λόγος γὰρ ἐκεῖνος, καὶ τοῦτο ὡς ῥῆμα καὶ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ ἀπεστάλη. καὶ διὰ τὸ εἰδέναι, ὅτι τὰ παρὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἢ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος λεγόμενα λέγεται καὶ παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς διὰ τὸ ἓν θέλημα, τὰ τοιαῦτα κεῖται ῥήματα. οὔτε γὰρ ἀγνοεῖ ἢ πέμπεται ὡς δοῦλον, οὔτε ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ λαλεῖ ἢ ποιεῖ ἢ ἔρχεται ὡς ἀντίθεον. 6.16ν ὅτι οὐδεὶς ὁρᾷ τὸν θεὸν καὶ πατέρα, εἰ μὴ μόνος ὁ υἱὸς καὶ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, καὶ πρὸς τοὺς λέγοντας· οὐ γέγραπται οὖν, φησίν, ὅτι οἱ ἄγγελοι βλέπουσιν τὸ πρόσωπον τοῦ πατρός; ἡ κτίσις οὐχ ὁρᾷ τὸν θεὸν καὶ πατέρα οὕτως, ὡς ἔστιν· ἑτέρᾳ γὰρ φύσει τοῦτο ἀχώρητον καὶ ἀβάστακτον ὑπάρχει· καὶ πρὸς αὐτήν ἐστιν τό· «οὐδεὶς ὄψεταί μου τὸ πρόσωπον καὶ ζήσεται.» αἱ δὲ γραφαὶ λέγουσιν, ποτὲ μὲν τὸν υἱὸν μόνον, ποτὲ δὲ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα μόνον ὁρᾶν ἢ εἰδέναι τὸν θεὸν πατέρα, ἐπειδὴ ἐν μονάδι θεότητος ἡ τριάς, ὡς ἡνίκα ὁ σωτὴρ παρὰ Ἰωάννῃ λέγει· «οὐχ ὅτι τὸν πατέρα τις ἑόρακεν, εἰ μὴ ὁ ὢν ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ· οὗτος ἑόρακεν τὸν πατέρα.» ἔστιν δὲ ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ κατὰ φύσιν ὁ υἱὸς γεννητικῶς, καὶ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα ἐκπορευτικῶς· καὶ πάλιν· «οὐδὲ γὰρ τὸν πατέρα τις ἐπιγινώσκει, εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱός, καὶ ᾧ ἐὰν ὁ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψῃ,» καὶ ὡς ὅταν ἰδικῶς περὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος, ὡς προελέχθη, Παῦλος Κορινθίοις γράφει, καὶ ὡς Ἠσαῖας προφητεύει· «πνεῦμα σοφίας καὶ συνέσεως, πνεῦμα γνώσεως καὶ εὐσεβείας.» οὐ γέγραπται οὖν, φησίν, Ματθαίῳ ἀπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος· «ὁρᾶτε, μὴ καταφρονήσητε ἑνὸς τῶν μικρῶν τούτων· λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν, ὅτι οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτῶν ἐν οὐρανοῖς διὰ παντὸς βλέπουσιν τὸ πρόσωπον τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς;» ναί· ἀλλὰ βλέπουσιν, οὐχ ὅσος καὶ οἷός ἐστιν ὁ θεός, ἀλλὰ καθ' ὅσον αὐτοὶ χωροῦσιν. ὁ δὲ μονογενὴς καὶ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα διὰ τὸ ταὐτὸν τῆς θεότητος ὁρῶσιν οὕτως, ὡς ἔστιν ὁ ἀμεγέθης καὶ ἀνείδεος θεός. 6.17ν ὅτι τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα τὴν κτίσιν υἱοθεσίας ἀξιοῖ· αὐτὸ δὲ ἐκ τῆς ὑποστάσεως τοῦ θεοῦ ἐκπορεύεται. ἡ κτίσις ἡ λογική, ὅταν ἀξία γένηται ἀνακαινισμοῦ καὶ υἱοθεσίας, ὑπὸ τῆς πανδυνάμου χάριτος τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος τούτων ἀξιοῦται, ἐπειδὴ οὐ κτίσμα, ἀλλὰ θεὸς ὑπάρχει, οἷος ὁ κτίσας τὸ πρῶτον. 6.18ν ὅτι οὐχ ὑμνεῖ ὡς ἡ ἄλλη κτίσις· ἐπειδὴ αὐτὸ τῶν ὑμνημένων ἐστι. ἡ κτίσις 64 πᾶσα, ὁρατὴ καὶ ἀόρατος, ὀνομαστὶ προστάττεται ὑπὸ τῶν τριῶν παιδῶν Ἀνανία, Ἀζαρία καὶ Μισαὴλ ἐν τῇ Βαβυλωνίᾳ καμίνῳ ἀποτεθέντων ὑμνεῖν καὶ ὑπερυψοῦν τὸν θεὸν εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· ἔτι δὲ καὶ τὰ Χερουβὶμ καὶ ὁ θεϊκὸς θρόνος, ὃ ἐνταῦθα νοεῖται τὰ Σεραφίμ, δοξάζει ἅτε ὄντα καὶ αὐτὰ μέρος τῆς κτίσεως. ἔφασαν γὰρ οἱ αὐτοί· «εὐλογήμενος εἶ, ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῶν Χερουβίμ,» καὶ πάλιν ἀντὶ τοῦ μνημονεῦσαι τῶν Σεραφίμ· «καὶ εὐλογημένος εἶ ἐπὶ θρόνου τῆς βασιλείας σου, καὶ ὑπερύμνητος καὶ ὑπερυψούμενος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας.» ὁμοίως καὶ ὑπὸ τοῦ ∆αυίδ, ἐνεργουμένου ὑπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος, ἐν ρβʹ καὶ ἐν ρμηʹ ψαλμῷ παρακελεύεται ἡ κτίσις αἰνεῖν τὸ κύριον. τὸ δὲ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, ὡς καὶ ὁ υἱός, οὐ συνεμνημονεύθη, ἐπειδὴ καὶ αὐτὸ οὐ δημιούργημα, ἀλλὰ δημιουργός· οὐδὲ τῶν ὑμνούντων, ἀλλὰ τῶν ὑμνουμένων καὶ ὑπ' αὐτῶν τῶν Σεραφίμ ἐστιν τῶν σὺν πολλῷ φόβῳ περιεστώτων τὸ θεϊκὸν βῆμα καὶ συγκαλυπτόντων ταῖς πτέρυξιν ἑαυτὰ καὶ ἀμοιβαδὸν ἀνταναφωνούντων ἀσιγήτοις στόμασιν καὶ ἀκαταπαύστῳ φωνῇ τρίτον «ἅγιος» διὰ τὰς τρεῖς ὑποστάσεις, ἅπαξ «κύριος» διὰ τὴν μίαν κυριότητα· ἅπερ, ὅτι μάλιστα δείκνυσιν τὴν θεότητα τοῦ πανυμνήτου πνεύματος. Μακεδονιανοὶ δέ, φυλαττόμενοι καὶ οἷον δεδοικότες, μὴ περὶ αὐτοῦ ἢ προσήκοντά ποτε λέγοντες ὀφθῶσιν ἢ ἀπρόσηκα προέμενοι λάθωσιν, ἐπιβαίνουσιν ἄνευ δίκης ἑαυτοῖς ἐπιτρέποντες καὶ τῷ
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing from the previous section: ... which he must also,] when it is needed, make known to those who are worthy. And that Peter, as has been said before, wrote: the Spirit was sent from heaven; let it be understood in the way in which is understood: the Son was sent. For as that one was sent as Word, this one too was sent as utterance and Spirit of God. And because of knowing that the things said by Christ or by the Holy Spirit are said also by the Father, because of the one will, such words are set down. For neither is he ignorant or sent as a slave, nor does he speak or act or come from himself as a rival god. 6.16ν [Chapter title:] That no one sees the God and Father, except only the Son and the Holy Spirit; and against those who say: Is it not written then, he says, that the angels see the face of the Father? The creation does not see the God and Father thus, as he is; for to another nature this is uncontainable and unbearable; and toward it [creation] is the saying: 'no one will see my face and live.' But the Scriptures say sometimes that the Son alone, sometimes that the Holy Spirit alone sees or knows God the Father, since the Trinity is in a unity of Godhead, as when the Saviour says in John: 'not that anyone has seen the Father, except the one being from God; this one has seen the Father.' And the Son is from God according to nature in the manner of begetting, and the Holy Spirit in the manner of proceeding; and again: 'for neither does anyone know the Father, except the Son, and to whomever the Son may reveal'; and as when Paul writes to Corinthians specifically about the Holy Spirit, as was said before, and as Isaiah prophesies: 'spirit of wisdom and understanding, spirit of knowledge and godliness.' Is it not written then, he says, in Matthew from the Saviour: 'see, do not despise one of these little ones; for I say to you that their angels in heavens continually see the face of my Father who is in heavens'? Yes; but they see, not how great and of what sort God is, but so far as they themselves contain. But the only-begotten and the Holy Spirit, through the sameness of the Godhead, see thus, as he is, the God without magnitude and without form. 6.17ν [Chapter title:] That the Holy Spirit counts creation worthy of adoption; and it itself proceeds from the hypostasis of God. The rational creation, whenever it becomes worthy of renewal and adoption, is counted worthy of these by the all-powerful grace of the Holy Spirit, since it is not a creature, but is God, such as the one who created at first. 6.18ν [Chapter title:] That it does not hymn as the other creation does; since it itself is of the things hymned. All the creation [page number 64, debris], visible and invisible, is commanded by name by the three youths Ananias, Azarias and Misael, put away in the Babylonian furnace, to hymn and exalt God into the ages; and further also the Cherubim and the divine throne, by which here the Seraphim are understood, glorify, as being themselves also part of the creation. For the same ones said: 'blessed are you, the one sitting upon the Cherubim,' and again, instead of mentioning the Seraphim: 'and blessed are you upon the throne of your kingdom, and hymned above all and exalted above all into the ages.' Likewise also by David, worked upon by the Holy Spirit, in the 102nd and in the 148th psalm (LXX; English 103 and 148), the creation is exhorted to praise the Lord. But the Holy Spirit, as also the Son, was not mentioned along with them, since it too is not a thing crafted, but the craftsman; nor of those hymning, but of those hymned, even by the Seraphim themselves, who with much fear stand around the divine tribunal and cover themselves with their wings and in alternation call back with unsilenced mouths and unceasing voice three times 'holy' because of the three hypostases, once 'Lord' because of the one lordship; which things most of all show the Godhead of the all-hymned Spirit. pass_b_english: …when the time is right, make known to those who are worthy.

As for Peter having written, as was said before, that the Spirit was sent from heaven (1 Peter 1:12), let it be understood in the way that “the Son was sent” is understood. For as that one was sent as the Word, so this one too was sent as the utterance and Spirit of God. And such expressions are set down because we know that what is said by Christ or by the Holy Spirit is said also by the Father, because of the one will. For the Spirit is not ignorant, nor is he sent as a slave; nor does he speak or act or come of himself, as a rival to God.
That no one sees God the Father except the Son alone and the Holy Spirit; and against those who say, “Is it not written, then, that the angels see the face of the Father?”

Creation does not see God the Father as he is, for to a nature other than his this is beyond its capacity and beyond its strength to bear. To creation applies the word: “No one shall see my face and live” (Exodus 33:20).

But the Scriptures say that sometimes the Son alone, and sometimes the Holy Spirit alone, sees or knows God the Father, since the Trinity is in a unity of Godhead. So the Saviour says in John: “Not that anyone has seen the Father, except him who is from God; he has seen the Father” (John 6:46). Now the Son is from God by nature by way of begetting, and the Holy Spirit by way of procession. And again: “For no one knows the Father except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him” (Matthew 11:27). So too when Paul, as was said before, writes to the Corinthians specifically about the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 2:11), and when Isaiah prophesies: “A spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of knowledge and godliness” (Isaiah 11:2).

“Is it not written, then,” they say, “in Matthew, from the Saviour: ‘See that you do not despise one of these little ones; for I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father who is in heaven’ (Matthew 18:10)?” Yes; but they see, not how great God is or what he is, but as much as they themselves can take in. The Only-begotten and the Holy Spirit, because the Godhead is the same, see God, who is without magnitude and without form, as he is.
That the Holy Spirit makes creation worthy of adoption, while he himself proceeds from the hypostasis of God.

When rational creation becomes worthy of renewal and adoption, it is made worthy of these by the all-powerful grace of the Holy Spirit, since he is not a creature but God, such as he is who created it in the first place.
That he does not sing hymns as the rest of creation does, since he is himself among those to whom hymns are sung.

All creation, visible and invisible, is bidden by name to sing hymns to God and exalt him for ever by the three youths, Ananias, Azarias and Misael, who were cast into the furnace in Babylon (Daniel 3:57-88 LXX). Further, the Cherubim and the divine throne, by which the Seraphim are meant here, glorify him, since they too are part of creation. For the same youths said: “Blessed are you who sit upon the Cherubim” (Daniel 3:55 LXX); and again, instead of naming the Seraphim: “And blessed are you on the throne of your kingdom, praised above all and exalted above all for ever” (Daniel 3:54 LXX). Likewise David, moved by the Holy Spirit, bids creation praise the Lord in the hundred and third and the hundred and forty-eighth Psalms (Psalm 103:20-22; Psalm 148:1-12).

But the Holy Spirit, like the Son, was not named along with them, since he too is not a thing made but the Maker; nor is he among those who sing hymns, but among those to whom hymns are sung, even by the Seraphim themselves. With great fear they stand around the divine judgment seat, covering themselves with their wings, and answering one another in turn with mouths that are never silent and a voice that never ceases, they cry “Holy” three times, for the three hypostases, and “Lord” once, for the one lordship (Isaiah 6:2-3). This, above all, shows the Godhead of the all-praised Spirit.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u16): retranslated. The old English mistranslated the opening (made 'the worthy' the thing revealed; 'such things are words'), turned 'uncontainable and unbearable' into 'incorporeal and uncontainable', broke off at 'And the only-begotten and the Holy Spirit...' and dropped the rest of 6.16, all of 6.17 except a stray 'makes creation worthy of adoption', and all of 6.18. Abbreviated references (Isa 11:2), (Matt 18:10) replaced by full names; new references checked against the KJV text.

choices.english: …when the time is right, make known to those who are worthy
choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence; the previous section ends ἃς χρὴ καὶ. Only the words this section holds are translated, opened with '…'.
Accusative with infinitive standing as a topic; ἀπεστάλη ἀπ' οὐρανοῦ τὸ πνεῦμα paraphrases 1 Peter 1:12 (πνεύματι ἁγίῳ ἀποσταλέντι ἀπ' οὐρανοῦ), so it is given as indirect speech with the reference.
The Spirit does not act on his own as one set against God; 'opponent' alone loses the 'god' in the compound.

choices.english: beyond its capacity and beyond its strength to bear
choices.why: χωρέω is the verb used again below of what the angels 'take in'; the old 'incorporeal' was not in the Greek.

choices.english: “Is it not written, then,” they say
choices.why: φησίν reports the objector named in the chapter title (πρὸς τοὺς λέγοντας); 'they say' keeps the objection theirs, not Scripture's.

choices.english: such as he is who created it in the first place
choices.why: The Spirit is God of the same kind as the first Creator; the clause does not say the Spirit was that Creator alone.
βῆμα is the raised seat of a ruler or judge; Didymus uses it for the throne of Isaiah 6.

choices.term: ἐν ρβʹ καὶ ἐν ρμηʹ ψαλμῷ
choices.english: in the hundred and third and the hundred and forty-eighth Psalms (Psalm 103:20-22; Psalm 148:1-12)
choices.why: Greek Psalm 102 = English 103; 148 is the same in both. Checked by verse text: both bid the works of the Lord and all creation to praise him.
The Song of the Three Youths exists only in Greek Daniel; cited with LXX numbering as elsewhere in the library, checked by hand.
64 is a printed page number in the copy-text, skipped.

choices.term: παρακελεύεται ἡ κτίσις αἰνεῖν τὸ κύριον
choices.why: τὸ κύριον (neuter article) is read as τὸν κύριον, 'the Lord'; the neuter is a slip in the copy-text.

choices.english: give themselves leave to attack even the …
choices.why: The sentence runs into the next section (κεφαλαίῳ τῷδε, 'this chapter'); only the words this section holds are translated, ending with '…'.
